title: More voltage between plates
hook: Change voltage magnitude and predict electric-field magnitude.
misconception: electric-field magnitude stays fixed when voltage magnitude doubles.
objective: Apply E = abs(V)/d to compare electric-field magnitude when voltage magnitude changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With ideal parallel plates at fixed separation ignoring edge effects, E = abs(V)/d. When voltage magnitude doubles, electric-field magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model E = abs(V)/d; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider ideal parallel plates at fixed separation ignoring edge effects, with a nonzero initial result. If voltage magnitude triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on electric-field magnitude?
recall.why: Apply E = abs(V)/d under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
